themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints in CD 318 surged to 7 THIS WEEK, a 5500% spike from the 8-week baseline average of 0.1 complaints per week, suggesting a coordinated campaign or sudden enforcement gap affecting storefront and street-level signage.
evidence: 7 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 20.79 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Represents most dramatic percentage spike across all tracked 311 categories in district
reporting_angles: Document the specific locations and types of illegal postings—are they political, commercial, or gang-related?
Interview 311 analysts and enforcement officers about whether this reflects a real surge or a sudden public awareness campaign

themes_detail.label: Street Noise & Vehicle Disruptions
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints jumped 376% to 25 complaints LAST WEEK (vs 5.2 weekly average), while vehicle noise spiked 196% to 10 complaints 2 WEEKS AGO (vs 3.4 weekly average), signaling a pattern of escalating noise enforcement gaps or new sources of disturbance.
evidence: Noise - Street/Sidewalk: 25 complaints last week vs 5.2 weekly average (z-score 3.84)
Noise - Vehicle: 10 complaints 2 weeks ago vs 3.4 weekly average (z-score 2.9)
Two overlapping noise categories spiking suggests systemic issue rather than isolated incident
reporting_angles: Map complaint clusters to identify hotspot neighborhoods within Flatlands/Canarsie—are they near highways, bars, or construction zones?
Interview residents about which times of day are most affected and whether NYPD noise enforcement has changed

themes_detail.label: Traffic Congestion Complaints Tripled
themes_detail.summary: Traffic complaints in CD 318 surged 300% to 4 complaints LAST WEEK versus 1.0 weekly average, suggesting either new congestion sources or emerging pattern of commuter frustration worth investigating.
evidence: 4 traffic complaints last week vs 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score 3.46)
300% spike represents one of highest percentage increases across all complaint types
Coincides with illegal parking complaints remaining highest overall category (2721 over 90 days)
reporting_angles: Investigate whether recent development activity (366 DOB permits filed, including 45 new buildings) is causing construction-related gridlock
Document commute times on major corridors (e.g., Flatbush Avenue near rezoning application area) to quantify real-world impact

themes_detail.label: Smoking/Vaping in Public Spaces Rising
themes_detail.summary: Smoking or vaping complaints jumped 122% to 5 complaints THIS WEEK from a 2.2 weekly average, the only emerging health-related behavior spike in the district and a potential indicator of enforcement changes or new concentration in specific public venues.
evidence: 5 smoking/vaping complaints THIS WEEK vs 2.2 weekly average (z-score 3.32)
122% increase in single week represents sharp departure from baseline
Suggests either new enforcement push or emerging congregation point
reporting_angles: Identify whether complaints cluster around schools, parks, or transit hubs
Interview Parks Department or NYC Department of Health about whether there has been a recent enforcement emphasis or public awareness campaign

themes_detail.label: Elevator Maintenance Backlog Signal
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints peaked 3 WEEKS AGO at 8 complaints (256% above the 2.2 weekly average), suggesting potential housing code compliance issues or maintenance delays affecting multi-unit buildings in the district.
evidence: 8 elevator complaints 3 weeks ago vs 2.2 weekly average (z-score 3.22)
256% spike indicates significant disruption to building infrastructure
Correlates with 366 DOB alteration filings, suggesting active building work may have disrupted elevator service
reporting_angles: Survey buildings with multiple elevator complaints to assess whether repairs are delayed by supply chain or contractor availability issues
Interview Housing Preservation Development about whether elevator inspection backlogs exist post-pandemic
